notes: Lensfun/geometry can refuse GPU Micro Grain but CPU still works. Record route rather than marking that case skipped; use neutral geometry and lens off for an explicit GPU Micro control where needed.
summary: The driver times all three Denoise methods, but does not apply a recipe per method or establish that each actually changed the picture.
evidence: seed has no Denoise-specific branch and the method loop uses app defaults after resets. The single module ON/OFF screenshot signature goes through changeState, which hard-codes Clean Grain. The skip helper checks Edge colour but only enabled repairs and omits the frontend's other eligibility checks, including non-Bayer, incomplete Bayer cells and authored SDR. Explicit nonzero defaults and all three selectors are wired, but visible changes per method are not statically verified.
proposed_fix: On IMG_0790.CR2, seed and hash exact per-method control maps; use the same maps on IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW. Clean Grain: {method:'clean_grain',amount:0.90,luminance:0.85,color_noise:0.90,detail_recovery:0.35,finest_noise:0.75,fine_noise:0.70,medium_noise:0.65,coarse_noise:0.60,grain_evenness:1,color_splotches:1,clean_splotches:true,clean_fringes:true,protect_color_edges:false,splotch_size:'small'}. Simple: {method:'standard',amount:0.90,luminance:0.85,color_noise:0.90,detail_recovery:0.35,finest_noise:0.75,fine_noise:0.70,medium_noise:0.65,coarse_noise:0.60}. Micro Grain: {method:'micro_grain',micro_luminance:0.85,micro_color:0.85,micro_detail:0.35}. Start each OFF, apply just that map, then compare settled ON and OFF signatures separately before timing. Use microGrainUnavailable(current lane) for skipped rows.
check: H3 and noisy-photo Fit plus large 100%: assert each eligible method changes pixels against its own OFF control, record no_op per failed method, and retain the default Clean Grain recipe for cross-module probes.

summary: At native zoom, a cached GPU Micro Grain tile can keep showing the previous slider settings.
evidence: The Micro tile cache key contains fitKey, frame size, working space and region but not microLuminance, microColor or microDetail. The hit copies final resolved pixels and returns before writeMicroGrainRegion. setDenoiseControls replaces the controls without dropping tiles; the same Micro fitKey survives live changes. The Fit reduced key does include all three sliders.
proposed_fix: Add all three Micro controls to the final RGB tile key, leaving reusable Bayer and demosaic keys unchanged.
check: Large 100% and eligible GPU Micro source: warm a visible tile, move one Micro control without panning, require a changed exact signature and match a fresh render at the new value.

notes: Phase 2 owns the findings file only; prepare the output-changing patch in Phase 4.
summary: At native zoom, GPU Clean Grain can reuse an old colour correction after settings change, even across a packed-colour to brightness-only layout change.
evidence: The bounded Clean Grain tile key uses fitKey instead of the computed fineGrainPixelControls endpoint key. The fit only includes a subset of controls (amount, luminance, recovery, fine and medium bands and whether a fit is required), not splotch reach, fringe/edge protection, colorNoise, coarse/finest bands or the actual grainEvenness value. An existing denoiseTile hit only checks width and height, so it can return pixels from the old settings or an incompatible rgba32uint versus rgba16float endpoint texture. Fit's reducedGrainKey already uses endpoint controls.
proposed_fix: Include fineGrainPixelControls(controls,true) and the packed layout in bounded Clean Grain tile identity; keep blend-only Color Splotches (and evenness only where truly represented by the endpoints) out of the key.
check: At 100% with GPU Clean Grain, warm the same tile and switch Small to Large, toggle edge/fringe protection and edit Color Noise. Exact pixels must track the selected controls and equal a fresh render; also cover packed to unpacked.
